status: Closed — fixed; imported-record bundle lane reverified
area: Git governance / task import record commit
finding: `tasks import --write` for new planned task cards can create task-owned ledger and task-event files that `git record-commit` refuses to combine across tasks, while a per-task staged record commit is then blocked by the pre-commit hook as `ATM_CROSS_TASK_MUTATION_BLOCKED` because the imported planned task record is treated as an active task-owned mutation.
expectedBehavior: Task-import ledger records should have a governed record-only commit lane that can commit one or more newly imported planned task records, or the import command should emit an explicit commit/recovery command that pre-commit accepts. A normal planning import should not require emergency no-verify.
evidenceOrRepro: On 2026-07-30, importing ATM-GOV-0269 through ATM-GOV-0273 succeeded with `ATM_TASKS_IMPORT_WRITE_READY`. `node atm.mjs git record-commit --actor codex-git-series-captain --message ... --json` then failed with `ATM_CROSS_TASK_MUTATION_BLOCKED` for the five task histories. Splitting to one staged task and retrying record-commit failed in pre-commit with `ATM_CROSS_TASK_MUTATION_BLOCKED` for the single newly imported planned task record.
followUp: Revalidated on 2026-09-03 with tests/cli/git-record-commit.test.ts: a newly imported planned task ledger plus its matching import transition passes record-commit dry-run, commits through the real pre-commit hook, includes the imported ledger in HEAD, and leaves no staged residue. The test describes this as the low-risk import-record bundle lane; no additional source repair is required.
